aliasGroups.label: C
aliasGroups.rationale: Reviewed records identify the C programming language. Language influence, host syntax and implementation-language assertions remain distinct edges, not identity proof for C++.

aliasGroups.label: C++
aliasGroups.rationale: All variants explicitly label the C++ language; CUDA C/C++ extension and C with Classes remain separate.

aliasGroups.label: Ruby
aliasGroups.rationale: Named Ruby language, not Rails framework or a specific Ruby implementation/runtime.

aliasGroups.label: Python
aliasGroups.rationale: Named Python language; source claims about its reference implementation do not turn the language into CPython.

aliasGroups.label: GCC
aliasGroups.rationale: Same named compiler collection, C/C++ frontend roles preserved in variants.

aliasGroups.label: Clang
aliasGroups.rationale: Same named compiler frontend with distinct C and CUDA compilation assertions.

aliasGroups.label: LLVM
aliasGroups.rationale: Named compiler infrastructure, not Clang or nvcc.

aliasGroups.label: Unix
aliasGroups.rationale: Named Unix OS family; source implementation/history assertions preserved.

aliasGroups.label: CPU
aliasGroups.rationale: Generic CPU processor class, not host role, GPU or instruction set.

aliasGroups.label: Operating system
aliasGroups.rationale: OS definition identifies the general software concept; optical mount_interface integrates_with the same general operating system and exposes filesystem data. Not an OS-specific implementation.

aliasGroups.label: Linux
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records explicitly type Linux as an OS/platform. Source edges describe Docker support, OS services, optical media and ext4 use. Linux application sandboxing and Linux kernel remain separate.

aliasGroups.label: Microsoft Windows
aliasGroups.rationale: Windows/Microsoft Windows OS records: Docker platform, OS services/NTFS, optical version family and volume management. Named Windows versions and sandbox implementations are not merged.

aliasGroups.label: Go
aliasGroups.rationale: Both Python records identify the named programming language: Grumpy targets Go and Python influenced Go; Kubernetes identifies Go as its implementation language. Influence is a relationship, not a separate language identity.

aliasGroups.label: .NET Common Language Runtime
aliasGroups.rationale: Sandbox names .NET Common Language Runtime and its CAS/security role; VM source names the same managed process runtime. Roles remain in original variants.

aliasGroups.label: Sandbox
aliasGroups.rationale: OS relationships[313] provides foundational isolation mechanisms; sandbox definition identifies the security mechanism. VM software-sandbox use case remains scoped.

aliasGroups.label: Java Virtual Machine
aliasGroups.rationale: Python relationships[310] runs Jython on Java VM; VM relationships[33] explicitly classifies Java Virtual Machine as a process VM. Python VM is excluded.

aliasGroups.label: Kubernetes
aliasGroups.rationale: All three source definitions identify the Kubernetes platform; K8s is its abbreviation.

aliasGroups.label: Virtual Machine
aliasGroups.rationale: The Docker abbreviation and both full-name records refer to the VM concept, not to a particular VM instance.

aliasGroups.label: Linux Namespaces
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records describe the Linux kernel isolation mechanism; Kubernetes resource namespaces are excluded.

aliasGroups.label: Linux cgroups
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records describe the Linux kernel control-group mechanism.

aliasGroups.label: Application Dependency
aliasGroups.rationale: Singular/plural records describe software dependencies bundled with an application; the library subtype remains separate.

aliasGroups.label: OpenShift
aliasGroups.rationale: Spelling variants identify the same named OpenShift platform in both source definitions.

aliasGroups.label: FreeBSD jail
aliasGroups.rationale: Singular/plural records identify the same named FreeBSD jail technology.

aliasGroups.label: Application Portability
aliasGroups.rationale: Definitions all describe moving packaged applications between execution environments; infrastructure/API portability remains distinct.

aliasGroups.label: Docker
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records explicitly name the Docker container platform. The nginx survey mention stays source-scoped.

aliasGroups.label: Container
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records define the isolated application runtime unit; image artifacts, orchestration units and VMs remain separate.

aliasGroups.label: Container runtime
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records define the software that executes container lifecycles; CRI access is a Kubernetes-specific variant field.

aliasGroups.label: Hypervisor
aliasGroups.rationale: All records name the hardware-sharing virtualization layer; ISA/x86 records describe hardware support for the same concept.

aliasGroups.label: JavaScript
aliasGroups.rationale: These records explicitly identify the JavaScript language, not its engines, ECMAScript specification, or runtimes. Preserve each implementation/use assertion.

aliasGroups.label: CSS
aliasGroups.rationale: All records identify the Web styling language. React Native record describes a comparison to CSS, NOT use of CSS; retain its distinction edge and separate native styles.

aliasGroups.label: React
aliasGroups.rationale: The named React UI library, not React Native or Next.js. Framework/library taxonomy disagreements are preserved in original records.

aliasGroups.label: Next.js
aliasGroups.rationale: Explicitly named React-based Next.js framework in both documents.

aliasGroups.label: React Native
aliasGroups.rationale: Named native-UI framework, separate from React library and browser frameworks.

aliasGroups.label: HTTP
aliasGroups.rationale: Named HTTP protocol family. Python HTTP-support module remains separate, as do HTTP versions and transports.

aliasGroups.label: Internet Protocol (IP)
aliasGroups.rationale: Named IP protocol family, not an IP address, packet, version, or TCP/IP architecture.

aliasGroups.label: IPv6
aliasGroups.rationale: Explicit Internet Protocol version 6 records, distinct from generic IP and IPv4.

aliasGroups.label: TCP
aliasGroups.rationale: Named Transmission Control Protocol, not the historical Transmission Control Program, TCP segment or protocol suite.

aliasGroups.label: Router
aliasGroups.rationale: Generic IP forwarding device; the IPv6-specific router subtype and access point remain separate.

aliasGroups.label: Network routing
aliasGroups.rationale: Path computation/selection across networks. React URL routing and packet-forwarding-specific records are NOT this identity.

aliasGroups.label: Firewall
aliasGroups.rationale: Generic network security traffic control system. Switch plug-in firewall-function record remains scoped.

aliasGroups.label: Packet analyzer
aliasGroups.rationale: Same network packet inspection tool category, not a specific analyzer implementation.

aliasGroups.label: Cloud computing
aliasGroups.rationale: Named network-delivered computing service model, not a deployment location or universal VM requirement.

aliasGroups.label: CUDA
aliasGroups.rationale: Named NVIDIA GPU computing platform; not toolkit, runtime API, CUDA C extension or GPU hardware.

aliasGroups.label: Lua
aliasGroups.rationale: Named Lua language, not Torch7 library or Lua runtime implementation.

aliasGroups.label: Network switch
aliasGroups.rationale: Both source records explicitly identify the generic networking device; router and multilayer-switch subtype are separate.

aliasGroups.label: Wireless LAN (WLAN)
aliasGroups.rationale: Generic wireless local-area network category, not Wi-Fi brand, IEEE standard or campus network as a whole.

aliasGroups.label: Assembly language
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records explicitly identify symbolic assembly language as a representation of machine instructions; specific assembler toolchains and ISAs remain separate.

aliasGroups.label: Instruction Set Architecture (ISA)
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records define the programmer-visible instruction/register/exception contract; the x86 record is the generic concept variant inside the x86 graph, not the x86 ISA itself.

aliasGroups.label: UDP
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records identify the User Datagram Protocol, the connectionless datagram transport; protocol-version and OSI layer mentions remain in variants.

aliasGroups.label: ICMP
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records identify the Internet Control Message Protocol carried with IP.

aliasGroups.label: DNS
aliasGroups.rationale: All five records identify the Domain Name System naming/lookup service; Kubernetes cluster DNS and DNS-based attacks remain separate scoped records.

aliasGroups.label: Telnet
aliasGroups.rationale: All three records identify the Telnet remote-terminal protocol that Mirai-class botnets scan.

aliasGroups.label: SSH
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records identify the Secure Shell remote-access protocol; key-exchange and git-transport mentions remain scoped.

aliasGroups.label: IPv4
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records identify Internet Protocol version 4 with 32-bit addressing.

aliasGroups.label: Internet of Things
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records identify the Internet of Things device domain; Mirai-family targets and asset categories remain separate records.

aliasGroups.label: ARM architecture
aliasGroups.rationale: All three records identify the ARM processor architecture, including as a Mirai-family build target.

aliasGroups.label: GitHub
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records identify the GitHub source-hosting service; the Mirai record documents the public source release.

aliasGroups.label: Redis
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records identify the Redis key-value server; the Gayfemboy record describes abuse of unauthenticated Redis instances.

aliasGroups.label: SELinux
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records identify the SELinux Linux security module; the Gayfemboy record lists it among target-hardening controls.

aliasGroups.label: Proof of work
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records identify the proof-of-work consensus/anti-abuse mechanism; Bitcoin-specific difficulty and reward parameters remain separate records.

aliasGroups.label: Hashcash
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records identify the Hashcash proof-of-work system.

aliasGroups.label: Bitcoin
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records identify the Bitcoin cryptocurrency network; Bitcoin-scoped blocks, transactions, nodes and wallets remain separate records.

aliasGroups.label: SHA-256
aliasGroups.rationale: All six records identify the SHA-256 hash algorithm; BitTorrent v2 and Bitcoin usage assertions remain as edges, not identities.

aliasGroups.label: Digital signature
aliasGroups.rationale: All three records identify the digital-signature primitive; specific schemes such as ECDSA remain separate.

aliasGroups.label: Public key
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records identify the openly distributed asymmetric public key; the digital-signature source's narrower verification-key record remains separate.

aliasGroups.label: Private key
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records identify the secret asymmetric private key; the digital-signature source's narrower signing-key record remains separate.

aliasGroups.label: ECDSA
aliasGroups.rationale: All three records identify the Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm.

aliasGroups.label: Cryptographic hash function
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records identify the general cryptographic hash-function primitive; specific algorithms such as SHA-1 and SHA-256 remain separate.

aliasGroups.label: scrypt
aliasGroups.rationale: All three records identify the memory-hard scrypt password KDF / proof-of-work algorithm.

aliasGroups.label: Sybil attack
aliasGroups.rationale: All three records identify the Sybil multiple-identity attack pattern.

aliasGroups.label: Byzantine fault tolerance
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records identify Byzantine fault tolerance for arbitrary/malicious failures.

aliasGroups.label: Elliptic-curve cryptography
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records identify elliptic-curve public-key cryptography; ECDSA is a specific scheme within it.

aliasGroups.label: Distributed system
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records identify the general distributed-system concept; API-style and object-system records remain scoped.

aliasGroups.label: Denial-of-service attack
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records identify the availability-disrupting denial-of-service attack category; DDoS and specific techniques remain separate records.

aliasGroups.label: Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS)
aliasGroups.rationale: All three records identify the distributed, multi-source denial-of-service attack category.

aliasGroups.label: Malware
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records identify the malicious-software category; VM-threat and sandbox-analysis variants remain scoped.

aliasGroups.label: Botnet
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records identify the remotely controlled network of compromised devices; individual botnet families and historical botnets remain separate records.

aliasGroups.label: Mirai
aliasGroups.rationale: All four records identify the Mirai IoT/Linux botnet malware family; specific variants such as Satori remain separate records.

aliasGroups.label: Availability
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records identify service availability, the security property DoS attacks target.

aliasGroups.label: OSI model
aliasGroups.rationale: Both records identify the seven-layer OSI networking reference model; the TCP/IP-source record typed reference_model is protected from merging by the claim/reference safeguard.

OS:vm.label: Virtual machine (OS taxonomy)
OS:vm.rationale: OS relationships[317] connects virtual_machine to vm as same_concept_family; they are not merged.

Python:vm.label: Python virtual machine
Python:vm.rationale: Python relationships[193-194] identifies CPython bytecode runtime, not a generic system VM.

sandbox:linux.label: Linux application sandboxing
sandbox:linux.rationale: Sandbox relationships[25-27] identifies an implementation built on seccomp/cgroups/namespaces, not the Linux OS.

Python:namespace.label: Python Namespace
Python:namespace.rationale: Python runtime name binding is not Kubernetes resource grouping.

sandbox:isolation.label: Sandbox Isolation
sandbox:isolation.rationale: Sandbox security property is broader than VM-environment separation.

virtual_machine:isolation.label: VM Isolation
virtual_machine:isolation.rationale: VM environment separation remains distinct from generic sandbox security property.

sandbox:ios.label: iOS/iPadOS sandboxing
sandbox:ios.rationale: Source implementation record is the application sandbox, not the OS product.

Docker:host.label: Docker Host
Docker:host.rationale: Docker host can be a physical machine or VM; the VM document explicitly defines host as a physical machine.

virtual_machine:host.label: VM Host
virtual_machine:host.rationale: Physical host role retained separately from the broader Docker host role.

Kubernetes:namespace.label: Kubernetes Namespace
Kubernetes:namespace.rationale: Kubernetes resource grouping is not Linux kernel isolation.

declinedMerges.rationale: OS same_concept_family edge[317] must survive; Python bytecode runtime relationships[193-194] are not system-VM identities.
Linux application sandboxing implementation, Linux OS and Linux kernel have distinct scopes.
Security mechanism and software-sandbox use-case record remain distinct.
Generic logical storage, Docker persistence and Kubernetes mounted storage are not synonyms.
Optical filesystem remains distinct from generic filesystem; no speculative identity is introduced.
System-image relationship[3] is conditional on all relevant state being on disk, not an identity; optical relationship[0] is classification.
Docker image is a product-specific artifact; the other record is OCI-oriented and generic. Keep the narrower/broader distinction and add a typed editorial edge.
The source distinguishes orchestration technology from a cooperating-daemon cluster and a cluster grouping. Do not erase that distinction based on the shared Docker Swarm label.
The generic source record does not explicitly identify AIX; insufficient evidence for an identity merge.
Generic Virtuozzo versus specifically branded Parallels Virtuozzo Containers may carry product/version scope; retain both.
Docker service is an orchestration abstraction; Kubernetes Service is a network abstraction.
Product-specific storage objects have different scopes and lifecycles.
Linux kernel process isolation and Kubernetes API resource grouping are different concepts.
Identical labels hide different physical/virtual host scopes; split the previous automatic merge.
Container, Kubernetes, and general computer-cluster scopes are not identical.
General kernel, Linux implementation, shared-kernel model, and sharing mechanism are not identities.
Application portability, infrastructure/API portability, and process-VM platform independence are different scopes.
Keep generic activities separate from Kubernetes-specific mechanisms or example workloads.
Runtime unit, image artifact, Pod grouping, VM abstraction/subtypes, runtime category and implementations are not synonyms.

audit.policy: Records with the same normalized label across files are one concept (exact match only, no fuzzy similarity); people, evidence records, ambiguous words and declined pairs stay apart. Original records and all parallel source edges retained. Unusable files, records and edges are skipped and listed in warnings/skippedSources. Editorial edges do not repair or endorse source claims.
